lines: The bougainvillea goes purple-grey now. Still pretty. Score: nine.
Counted the pots on Henri's balcony. Fourteen. He has names for six.
Tomorrow: two laps, one croissant, repot the basil. Written down.
Jasmine o'clock. You smell it before you see it.
My grandmother said blue hour is when the flowers gossip.
Rosé the colour of the oleanders. Coincidence? No.
Lemon tree by the fountain. Counted eleven lemons. Twelve tomorrow.
Plan for later: shower, dance, sleep. In that order. Mostly.
Glass in one hand, a sprig of mint in the other. Balance.
The sea goes blue, the lamps go gold. Good trade.
Watered my rosemary at six. It looks smug about it.
First sip. Feet tingling. Six laps done. Top day.
Papa taught me to count waves. I still do. Forty so far.
Bougainvillea on the kiosk. Three colours on one wall. Greedy.
Tomorrow I run past the lemon trees first. Best smell on the loop.
Odile gave me a cutting of her lavender. It lives in a mug now.
Five lamps on. Six. Seven. The promenade is waking up for night.
Note to self: buy a bigger pot for the little olive.
Santé to the jasmine. It worked hard today.
My brother and I raced to this railing as kids. I won. Mostly.
The cypresses go black against the blue. Like paper cut-outs.
Saturday plan: market, peaches, a new pot of thyme. Lovely.
One glass, two olives, three songs. Then home.
Petals on the railing. Pink ones. The wind delivers.
Every window box on this street has a name. I am learning them.
Tiny lemon slice in the rosé. Henri's idea. Excellent idea.
That palm has a new frond. I watched it unroll all week.
Lap count today: six. Flower count: lost track at sixty.
Mamie said: one flower a day and you are never in a hurry.
Camille says my balcony looks like a jungle. Thank you, Camille.
Blue, then bluer, then lamps. I know this one by heart.
Tomorrow I will finally learn the name of that yellow flower.
Cheers, string lights. Right on time, as ever.
Last bee of the day, heading home. Same, bee. Soon.
The geraniums on the café look orange in this light. Magic.
Planting tulips in the spring. Ordered them already. Forty.
My papa toasts with his left hand. So do I. Family thing.
Breathing in. Sea, salt, jasmine. Three things. Lovely.
Little plan: sunrise from the top step tomorrow. Six sharp.
The rosé is cold, the stones are warm. Perfect pair.
Ten minutes at this railing. I timed it. Worth every one.
The lemon tree outside my door has one flower. One. Brave.
Glass of pink, sky of blue. Very French of me.
Bougainvillea petals are paper-thin. I checked. Twice.
Tomorrow's errand: string for the sweet peas. They want to climb.
Lucie toasts with a clink. I toast with two clinks. Better.
Counting lit windows. Nine. Ten. Henri just made eleven.
My aunt grows lemons in Menton. Size of fists. Sends photos.
The fountain sounds louder at blue hour. Same water, more echo.
Rosé, string lights, a good stretch earlier. Top marks.
Picked a fig on the way. Ate it before the corner. No regrets.
Ma soeur and I named every star here once. Mostly after cakes.
Sip, smile, sip. My evening routine. Very strict.
The oleanders are closing up. Goodnight, oleanders.
Thursday plan: help Henri with the big lemon pot. Two people job.
Lamp light on the water. Long golden lines. Six of them.
To the basil. To the thyme. To the mint. A full herb toast.
Swapped seeds with Odile. Marigolds for sunflowers. Fair deal.
Dusk smells like warm stone and lemon leaves. Bottle it, please.
Feet up on the crate. Glass up. Day well done.
Tomorrow's lap goes past the bakery and the roses. Both. Smart.
The palm fronds go still at blue hour. Like they listen.
Half a glass gone. Exactly half. I measured with my eye.
Pots on my steps: five. Plants in the pots: seven. Sharing.
The pink in my glass, the pink on the wall. Matching.
Sunday: picnic under the cypresses with my cousins. Ten of us.
Little pink cloud left over. Holding on. Good effort.
Marcel put a sprig of lavender by my glass. Ten points.
The lemon blossoms smell strongest now. Science. Probably.
Plan: dance three songs, not two. Ambitious. Doable.
Rosé after laps. Rosemary on the way home. Both good for me.
Stars: one. Two. A third one, shy. Welcome.
The window box on the corner has new petunias. Purple. Bold.
Chair warm, glass cold, lights on. Everything in order.
Théo says plants like music. Tonight they get Marcel's radio.
Next week: paint my pots blue. To match this hour exactly.
I stand here every evening. The bougainvillea grows a bit each time.
My cousin taught me santé with eye contact. Always eye contact.
The sky is the colour of plums. Ripe ones. Very nice.
Lemon tree, fig tree, olive tree. My street has a whole orchard.
Slow breath. Long look. Short run home later. Ideal.
Glass two? No. Glass one, part two. Different thing.
Mamie's rule: water at dawn, admire at dusk. Doing both.
Every evening the jasmine wins. It is not even a contest.
The ice clinks. The lights hum. The town is purring.
Picked a lemon leaf. Rubbed it. Smell that. Best perfume.
Tomorrow: seven laps. Eight if the sea looks extra nice.
One sip for each lap. Six laps. I will round down.
The roses by the steps are folding up. Little fists. Cute.
Planning a herb wall by my door. Twelve pots. Already counting.
Santé, blue hour. You are my favourite twenty minutes.
Last light on the cypress tips. Then gone. Then lamps. Lovely.
Sun gone. Sky still going. Bonus round.
Lamp one, lamp two, lamp three. Promenade, done.
A gull on the railing. Same pose as me. Copycat.
The railing is still warm. The sun left a tip.
Counting shutters closing. Six. Seven. Clack. Eight.
Biscuit is watching the gulls. The gulls are not worried.
Blue hour. My favourite colour, for a whole hour.
Twenty-two string lights. Twenty-three. Someone was late.
The clock says ten past eight. The sky says lovely.
Legs say rest. Eyes say look. Everyone wins.
That cat on the wall has not moved in an hour. Hero.
Somebody's lemon tree smells like tomorrow's tarte.
Stars. One. Two. Hold on, that one is a lamp.
I ran past this railing nine times today. Now I lean.
The awnings are rolling up. Goodnight, stripes.
Biscuit just sneezed at the sea. The sea forgave him.
Pink is gone. Blue is here. Very tidy handover.
Lucie, look! The water is the same colour as your bike.
A gull just landed on a lamp. Lamp king.
The tiles on the roofs go silver now. Every night.
One more minute here. Then exactly one rosé.
The church bell rang eight. I counted along. Correct.
Zinc roofs, blue sky. Everything matching tonight.
My shadow went home early. Lazy shadow.
Henri's window boxes look sleepy. Good, they worked hard.
The kiosk lights just came on. Ding. Like a toaster.
Railing, me, sea. In that order. Perfect.
The gulls have gone quiet. Even they say wow.
Calf stretch at the railing. Two birds, one railing.
If I lean any harder I will become a postcard.
The cat on the wall blinked at me. I blinked back. Friends.
Biscuit wants the gull. The gull wants the lamp. I want rosé.
The sea is breathing slower now. Same as me.
Eight shutters on that house. All blue. All shut. Neat.
Little waves, little lights, little me. Very nice.
Lucie's bell, far off. Ding. The town says hello.
Ten thousand steps, one railing. Fair exchange.
Palm tree waving. I wave back. It started it.
The fountain caught a lamp in it. Lucky fountain.
Blue on blue on blue. Somebody likes blue up there.
Rosé number one. Also rosé number last.
Marcel pours rosé like he is conducting an orchestra.
Santé to my legs. They did all the work.
Sip one. Sip two. Sip three is the best sip.
Feet up on the rail of the chair. Officially off duty.
The string lights are on. My glass has twenty-four in it.
Marcel brought olives. I did not ask. He just knows.
Santé to the cat on the wall. He is not drinking. Wise.
Two olives, one glass, zero laps. Lovely maths.
Odile waved from her bench. I waved with the glass. Careful.
Henri is telling the lemon tree goodnight. I heard him.
Clink with Lucie. Clink with Camille. Clink with the lamp.
Rosé tastes like a summer that never finished.
Biscuit is under my table. He is hoping. I see you, Biscuit.
A gull wants my olive. Monsieur, these are mine.
The ice clinks every time the fountain splashes. Duet.
I sat down. My legs said merci. Very polite legs.
Rosé, then dancing, then bed. The evening plan, in three.
Marcel says this is the good bottle. He says that every night.
My trainers are still on. They are invited too.
The chairs are all facing the sea. Correct chairs.
Théo and Camille are clinking. I clink at them from here.
Lamps on, rosé on, me on a chair. Everything on.
The tablecloth has little lemons on it. Henri approves.
That cat walked the whole wall. Ten out of ten, balance.
Café chairs are the best chairs. I have tested many.
Dance music warming up. Like me, an hour ago.
Rosé is just pink lemonade with a diploma.
Lucie says one more glass. Lucie says that a lot.
The fountain is lit now. It looks like it is showing off.
The olives are in a little bowl. Little bowls make me happy.
Biscuit got a crust from Marcel. Marcel is a soft touch.
My glass is sweating. I am not. Good evening for both.
Pink drink, blue hour, gold lamps. That is a flag.
Rest day tomorrow? No. Rest hour tonight? Yes.
Blue hour. The town gets quieter and kinder.
Day: run, café, run, railing, rosé. Today, five stars.
The lamps came on one by one. I said hello to each.
The clock tower is lit. It looks very proud.
Swallows overhead. Twelve. Fourteen. Too fast to count.
Every window going gold. Like a slow advent calendar.
The gulls are going to bed. Early birds, those.
Biscuit is leading Yusuf home. As usual.
Lucie said dancing at nine. I am ready at eight.
Blue hour is my cooldown. The sky cools down with me.
Today I counted 31 gulls. Personal best.
The kiosk awning is folded like a napkin. Very neat.
Odile says I glow. It is the string lights. And the laps.
One street, four shopfronts, a hundred lamps. Home.
Blue hour. Twelve minutes of it. I timed it last Tuesday.
Humming the song from last night. Bars one to eight, on repeat.
The sea went from pink to ink. I approve both.
Reading two pages before rosé. Chapter nine. A good one.
My book has a lighthouse in it. I keep looking up for one.
Rail, sea, sky, me. Four blues. Counted.
Lucie lent me her headphones. Accordion. Very correct.
Shoes off, socks on, sea air. A small festival.
I clap for the lamplighter in my head. Every night.
Bookmark: a café receipt. Marcel signed it. Collector's item.
Today: two laps, one lunch, zero rushing. Gold medal.
Learning to whistle. Gull one replied. Progress.
The kiosk radio is playing something with a trumpet. Yes.
Henri said my stride looks lighter. I will take it.
Sky is one shade off my running shirt. Close enough.
Sketching the fountain. Third try. The pigeon helped.
Writing tomorrow's route on my hand. Short. Pretty. Done.
Five deep breaths. Then rosé. Order matters.
Somebody upstairs is practising piano. Same tune, nicer each time.
String lights, check. Sea, check. Me, also check.
I saved Odile the corner seat. She waved twice. Worth it.
The water is so still the lamps have twins.
Leaning, not stretching. Big difference. Both nice.
A crossword clue for this: blue, quiet, lovely. Six letters?
Camille said my laps are her clock. Best compliment this week.
The bench behind me has three friends on it. Full house.
I keep a list of good sunsets. This week: four for four.
Ten minutes on this rail and my legs forgot the laps.
Théo asked my pace. I said happy. He wrote it down.
Listening to the lights hum. Very soft. Very good.
Gave my spare hair tie to a visitor. Good deed, number one.
Rosé, chair, string lights. My evening stretch routine.
Marcel poured mine before I sat down. A true artist.
Glass in one hand, crossword in the other. Busy woman.
Four across: pink evening drink, four letters. Too easy.
Santé, Lucie! Santé, Camille! Santé, little lamp!
Rosé the colour of the sky an hour ago. Neat trick.
Swapping books with Lucie. Mine has a map. Hers has a dog.
The accordion man started. My feet are already deciding.
Two sips, one story, one big laugh. The ratio is right.
Théo says cheers in four languages. I learned two tonight.
I told Marcel his olives are famous. He bowed. Twice.
One glass. I count sips like laps. Seven so far.
Camille brought cherries for the table. Instant favourite.
Napkin, pen, a tiny drawing of Biscuit. Gift for Yusuf.
Théo asked about my run. I said great. He said bravo.
Lucie's toast: to bells and legs. I will drink to that.
Writing a list of songs to dance to. Twelve. Maybe thirteen.
Marcel hums while he pours. Same song as yesterday. Lovely.
Camille complimented my scarf. I bought it for running. Ha.
Glass up for the builder. His window is on. Hard worker.
My bookmark is a postcard of this exact café. Very loyal.
The table wobbles. Théo fixed it with a sugar packet. Hero.
I say one glass. The glass says, we will see.
Small chat, big smile, cold glass. Five stars.
I learned a card trick for Léo. Practising on Camille.
Camille knows the words to this song. All of them. Wow.
Théo is counting the stars. I am counting his counting.
Marcel left a little extra in my glass. I saw. Merci.
Knitting club tomorrow. I am at row forty. A sock. Sort of.
Lucie and I clink every time a lamp flickers. Tradition.
Salted almonds. I count them too. Nine. Ten. Gone.
Théo said my laugh carries to the fountain. Good.
Passing the olives down the table. Sharing is a sport.
Marcel taught me to say rosé properly. I did it. Applause.
Lamps on at twenty past eight. Right on time.
Day total: two laps, three coffees, many hellos.
Every lamp has a little moth friend. Very sweet.
Song stuck in my head: the one from the kiosk radio.
I read on the bench, Henri reads on the bench. Book club.
Tomorrow I bake for the café. Lemon. Henri's lemons.
Evening routine: stretch, sit, sip, smile. Repeat.
Biscuit gave me a paw. A high five, basically.
Twenty-two seconds of total quiet just now. I counted.
Yusuf found the right song for the evening. As always.
Pre-ordered Lucie a croissant for tomorrow. Surprise.
Promenade at blue hour: forty steps of pure calm.
I wrote a tiny poem. Sea. Me. Tea. Wait, rosé.
My watch says rest. I agree with my watch.
The string lights did a little sway. Hello to you too.
Henri and Odile are holding hands on the bench. Ten points.
Learned three dance steps today. Testing them in an hour.
Sky the colour of my favourite pen. Writing that down.
Thanked the kiosk man for the paper. He thanked me back.
Today: zero rain, all sun, one lovely blue. Score: high.
Night is coming slowly. Very polite of it.
The breeze just arrived. Right on time.
Blue hour. Twenty minutes of it. Not wasting one.
Lap legs, railing arms, sea eyes. All accounted for.
First lamp just blinked on. Then four more. Counted.
Sea air in. Out. In. Best exercise of the day.
Salt on my lips, wind in my ponytail. Sorted.
Leaning here till the first star. Then rosé.
There. First star. Right over the zinc roofs.
Two stars now. They are racing. I like it.
Warm night, bare arms, no jacket. Score!
A little breeze lifts my fringe. Hello, breeze.
Cooling down at the railing. Heart rate: content.
The cypresses are swaying. Like they did a lap too.
Lavender on the breeze. Someone watered their pots.
Seven gulls on the rocks. Sorry, eight. A latecomer.
Silver sea, then ink blue sea. Both gorgeous.
Legs buzzing, sky glowing. Equal parts.
The swifts are doing laps. Faster than me. Fine.
An accordion, somewhere up the hill. Perfect.
String lights warming up. One, by one, by one.
The palms are whispering. Probably about my pace.
Warm stone, cool air. The ideal evening ratio.
Fifteen windows. Someone just got home.
Watching the water go dark. Slowly. Like a lid.
The breeze smells of jasmine. And a bit of bread.
Lucie's hair in this wind! Happy chaos.
I could lean here all night. I will lean ten minutes.
Fountain behind me, sea in front. Stereo.
A moth is doing laps of the lamp. Good form.
Rosé, glass one. Pace: slow. Very slow.
Marcel poured exactly to the line. A professional.
Ice clinking. The best little bell in town.
Sitting down for the first time since six. Lovely chair.
Santé, sky. Santé, sea. Santé, legs.
Olives: seven. I counted. Now: zero.
String lights above, rosé in hand. Full marks.
Camille and Théo clinked so loud I clinked too.
A breeze across the terrace. Glass stays cold.
Half a glass. Pacing it like a long run.
Toasts so far tonight: three. And rising.
Warm enough to sit out till midnight. Probably will.
Breadsticks and rosé. Recovery food. Official.
Dance floor count: two couples. Now three.
Pink cheeks. Running or rosé? Both.
I sip, I breathe, I sit. Lap time: irrelevant.
Lucie stole my olive. I stole her breadstick. Even.
Glass on the table, chin in my hand. Bliss mode.
The fountain sounds like it is clapping for us.
Little candle on the table. Flickering at my pace.
Two sips in and I already want to dance.
Blue hour. My favourite hour I don't run in.
Still in my running shoes. Still smiling.
Laps today: four. Smiles today: lost count.
Ten more minutes outside. Then ten more.
Evening rule: stop, look up, say wow. Wow. Done.
The town hums at this hour. Low and happy.
The breeze changed sides. Now it smells of the sea.
Sky so blue I want to keep some in a jar.
Every bench full, every lamp lit. Good town.
Odile waved her scarf at me. I waved my water bottle.
Yusuf on the phone. Biscuit on Yusuf's foot.
Warm evening, salt air, bare ankles. Summer, stay.
The cobbles are still warm. Barefoot? Tempting.
A cat crossed the square. Steady pace. Respect.
Someone is frying garlic. Very good someone.
Hair down after laps. The wind does the rest.
Little lights on the hill now. I count nine.
The fountain is the same blue as the sky. Twins.
Two children by the fountain, whispering wishes.
A coin in the fountain. Plink. Wish: top secret.
Léo waved from his window. Pyjamas already!
Someone left a ball by the fountain. Tomorrow's game.
Chalk hopscotch by the fountain. Eight squares. Hopped it.
Kids racing home for bath time. Good sprint form.
Laughter from a balcony. Best sound in town.
Kicked a stray ball back to the fountain step. Goal!
Splash, splash, splash. The fountain keeps my rhythm.
Bonne soirée! To everyone. All at once.
Swallows off, bats on. The evening shift change.
Bat count: three. Very quick. Very polite.
A breeze on my neck. Like a tiny round of applause.
Two taps on the railing when I finish. My own finish line.
Ponytail down. That means the day is officially closed.
Hair tie on my wrist now. Off duty, but ready.
Peeling an orange in one long curl. Nailed it tonight.
Tried standing still. My heels are still bouncing.
Retied my laces looser. Evening laces. Very relaxed.
Sandals now. My toes have never seen this hour before.
Walked backwards here from the café. Calves love it.
Each evening I pick one window and guess the dinner. Soup.
Water bottle half full. I call that optimistic.
Whispering my lap times to the sea. It keeps secrets.
Watch off, wrist free. I can tell time by the sky now.
Hamstring stretch. Upside down, the sea looks the same.
Probably the only person here who rests by walking fast.
Henri says my resting face is a smile. I checked. True.
This is where I make a wish for tomorrow's legs.
Humming while I stretch. Lower note, deeper stretch.
Ritual: one big yawn at the railing. Evening, officially.
Ankle circles. Ten each way. My ankles expect it now.
Promised to walk home slowly. I promised yesterday too.
Cap off. My hair is cap-shaped. Very fashionable.
A pebble from every lovely evening. My pocket is heavy.
Shirt inside out all day. Nobody noticed. Wonderful.
Waving at my route from up here. Bye, loop. See you at six.
One shoulder roll for every street I ran. Four streets.
Tried meditating here once. I meditated about croissants.
Socks pulled up high. Style or warmth? Both, I decide.
When I yawn, Biscuit yawns. We tested it. Twice.
My legs fell asleep before me. Fair enough, they ran.
Sit for five minutes, I said. I lasted three. Progress.
Elbows on the rail, chin on my hands. Thinking pose.
One slow lap of the railing. Walking. Very strange.
A morning person standing in the evening. How brave.
Lucie says I lean like I am stretching. I am. Always.
Talked to myself the whole run. Great company, honestly.
Glass of water first, then the pink. My only rule. Mostly.
First sip with my eyes closed. Opened them. Still lovely.
Turned my chair to face the sea. Every time. Marcel sighs.
One ice cube, never two. Marcel knows. Marcel always knows.
My knee is bouncing under the table. Lap seven, seated.
Folded my napkin into a little running shoe. Art.
Rosé in a running shirt. Elegant? Let us say yes.
Sandals under the table, toes wiggling. Off the clock.
My hair still smells of the sea breeze. Free perfume.
Last sip is always saved for the first star. Tradition.
Clinked with the empty chair. For whoever comes next.
Ordered in my best French. Marcel answered in English. Ha!
Keys tucked in my sock. Old runner habit. Never leaves.
Tried to look mysterious with my glass. Sneezed. Over.
The chair by the lamp is mine on Thursdays. Unofficially.
Glass in my left hand. Right hand free for waving.
Same order every night. Marcel acts surprised every night.
Shoes off under the table. Do not tell Marcel. He knows.
One joke every evening. Tonight's is about a tired sock.
Lucie laughs at my jokes first. Then she gets them.
Lip balm before the first sip. A small ceremony.
This chair has my shape now. Three summers of practice.
Tiny drumroll on the table before every toast. Brrrr.
Stretched a calf on Marcel's step. He gave it a score.
Cardigan on, glass in hand. A very cosy runner.
Loudest clinker in town, that is me. Ask anyone.
One spoon of Lucie's tarte. That is the deal. Two spoons.
Watch buzzed: time to stand. Sorry, watch. Busy sitting.
Turning the glass rings into little smiley faces. Habit.
The ice cube melted. I let it. Very relaxed of me.
Water bottle on the table, like a little chaperone.
Rosé tastes better after a shower. A fact. My fact.
Always beside the plant pot. It listens very well.
Napkin on my knee like a lady. Trainers on like a runner.
Wet hair, clean shirt, still a bit pink from running.
Evening walk. I keep almost jogging. Behave, legs.
Nodding at every lamp post from this morning. Old friends.
My evening speed is called stroll. Still learning it.
One clap when the last pink goes. One clap. Done.
White tiles only on the promenade. Since I was six.
Merci, legs, I say out loud. People smile. So do I.
Pocket check: keys, coins, one sweet. Ready for anything.
Humming as I walk. Out of tune. Very happy.
Ten years of hopping over that same crack. Still hopping.
Not racing that visitor. Just walking very well.
Evening plan: nothing fast at all. Wish me luck.
Tried a lazy evening once. I reorganised my shoes.
A postcard to myself every week. Fun mail on Mondays.
After eight my stride gets shorter. Like a clock winding down.
Smiling at strangers is my cooldown. Everyone smiled back.
Yawned. Covered it with my hand. The sky saw anyway.
Walked past the bakery. Waved at tomorrow's croissant.
Sleeves pulled over my hands. Cosiest hour of the day.
One little skip on the promenade, every evening. There.
Shower done, plait done, evening face on. Ready.
Fresh socks after laps. Best feeling a person can have.
Lap one. Henri's lemons: eleven. Yesterday: ten. Progress!
Bougainvillea on the blue door. Pinker than yesterday. Noted.
Three geraniums, two windows, one very happy cat.
The jasmine by the steps. I slow down for it. Every lap.
Lemon tree, lemon tree, palm, lemon tree. Good rhythm.
Odile's window box has a new red one. Welcome, little flower.
A lemon fell right in front of me. I said good morning to it.
Cypress, cypress, cypress. Like a row of tall friends.
The roses by the fountain opened overnight. Four of them.
Plan for today: laps, croissant, then buy basil. Three things.
Tomorrow I try the hill road. Maybe. Probably. Yes.
Tonight: dancing with Lucie. Right now: running. Very organised.
After this, flowers for my windowsill. Yellow ones.
Grand-mère ran in espadrilles. I have it easy.
Papa taught me to count lampposts. Still counting. Fourteen.
Maman calls on Sundays. I tell her the lemons are doing well.
My sister would love this light. Postcard, later. Note to self.
Breathe in: oleander. Breathe out: happiness. Repeat.
The lavender pots by the kiosk. I touch one each lap. For luck.
Lap three. The palms are combing their hair in the breeze.
Hello, terracotta pots. All nine of you, lined up so nicely.
Somebody planted marigolds by the steps. Who? Excellent work.
Five lemon trees on this street. I know each one personally.
Today's plan: water my own basil before Henri does it for me.
The fig tree has six new leaves. Yes, I counted. Of course.
The tomato plants on Théo's balcony stand up straighter each day.
Sunrise on the zinc roofs. Like toast. Very elegant toast.
I passed the olive tree three times. It did not move once.
Lap two done. The geraniums are cheering. Quietly, but still.
Future plan: a lemon tree of my own. Small one. On the balcony.
This weekend: bike ride with Lucie to the lavender fields.
Tomorrow: same route, one minute faster. The roses will see.
Later I pick up thyme for Maman's recipe. Do not forget, Inès.
When I was six I ran to the bakery in pyjamas. Some things stay.
My brother sleeps till nine. I bring him the morning in stories.
Dew on the petals. Dew on my shoes. Dew everywhere. Lovely.
Hibiscus by the post office. Big as a saucer. Good morning!
Counting window boxes. Twenty-two. A new record for this street.
The lemon tree by the café has one lemon shaped like a heart.
Bees already on the lavender. They are early too. Colleagues!
Henri's watering can is waiting by the door. He is next.
Morning glories! Named for exactly this. Very correct flowers.
That palm leans toward the sea. I lean toward the bakery.
I waved at a sunflower. It was facing the sun. Fair enough.
Plan: shower, coffee, then repot the little rosemary. Big day.
Next week the oleanders flower. I have it in my calendar.
Tonight, fresh lemons for the rosé. Henri promised me two.
Tomorrow I bring Henri the fern cutting. He will be so pleased.
Maman had a bougainvillea that ate the whole garage. Legend.
Grand-père whistled to his tomatoes. They loved it. Truly.
My first race medal hangs next to my basil. Both thriving.
My aunt sends lemon jam each spring. Today feels like that jar.
Petals on the promenade. Pink confetti for the first runner.
Lap one. The cypresses look like exclamation marks. Agreed!
A rose bush, a bench, a sleepy gull. Perfect little picture.
Lemons on the left, sea on the right. Best corridor in France.
Eight pots of herbs on that balcony. Nine if you count the chive.
The wisteria on the corner house. Like a purple waterfall. Slow.
The orange tree by the fountain smells like a Sunday.
